chapterTitle: Thermal Expansion and Change of State
modelAnswer: Initial volume V₀ = 5³ = 125 cm³. The temperature change is ΔT = 100 − 15 = 85 K. Using ΔV = βV₀ΔT with β = 9 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹, ΔV = (9 × 10⁻⁶)(125)(85) = 0.095625 cm³. Final volume = 125 + 0.095625 = 125.095625 cm³ (approximately 125.096 cm³).
stem: A solid cube of side length 5 cm at 15°C is heated. Calculate its (a) initial volume (b) increase in its volume (c) final volume at 100°C. (Coefficient of volume expansion of this solid is 9 × 10^-6 K^-1.)

chapterTitle: Thermal Expansion and Change of State
keyPoints: Evaporation occurs at the surface at any temperature
Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at its boiling point
Evaporation is slower and causes cooling; boiling forms bubbles
modelAnswer: Evaporation is a surface process that changes a liquid into vapour at any temperature; it is generally slow, uses energy from the surroundings, depends on factors such as surface area and temperature, and causes cooling. Boiling occurs throughout the liquid only at its boiling point, uses a continuous external heat source, forms bubbles, and is rapid once the boiling point is reached.
stem: Differentiate between evaporation and boiling of liquids.
